title: AI Practitioner Roadmap
description: A curated, stage-by-stage path from AI fundamentals and prompting to working confidently with assistants, coding tools, and building AI-backed applications.
audience: Anyone who wants to use AI effectively at work or in side projects — no machine-learning math required.
intro: This roadmap is built for practitioners, not researchers. The goal is confident, everyday fluency with AI tools and the judgement to know where they help and where they mislead.

stages.title: AI Foundations
stages.description: Understand what language models are, how they fail, and the vocabulary everyone now assumes you know. Ground concepts first — tools change monthly, concepts do not.
stages.milestone: You can explain what a language model does, why it hallucinates, and what the terms token, context window, and temperature mean.

steps.note: The conceptual base for every other step on this roadmap.

steps.title: AI Glossary
steps.note: Keep it open in a second tab — look terms up the moment you meet them.

stages.title: Prompting & Workflows
stages.description: The practical core of the roadmap: writing prompts that produce usable output, and turning repeated manual tasks into reusable prompt templates.
stages.milestone: You can take a vague request and turn it into a prompt that yields consistent, reviewable output — and refine it when the first attempt misses.

steps.title: Prompt Templates
steps.note: Try at least five templates against your own real work this week, not demo data.
Revisit the prompting modules with the templates you just tried — the lessons land differently with experience.

stages.title: Working with Assistants
stages.description: Go deeper with a specific assistant: its strengths, its interface, and how to structure ongoing work with it rather than one-off chats.
stages.milestone: You can use an assistant for multi-step work — research, drafting, review — with a repeatable process instead of ad-hoc prompting.

steps.note: Even if you use a different assistant, the workflow patterns transfer.

stages.title: AI Coding Tools
stages.description: For developers: use AI to write and review code without outsourcing your judgement. Learn what these tools are good at and where they quietly break things.
stages.milestone: You can pair with an AI coding tool on a real project — generating, testing, and reviewing code — while catching the mistakes it makes.

steps.note: Apply each exercise to a real repository of yours, not the course sample.

stages.title: Building AI Applications
stages.description: The final step for developers: wire a language model into a real backend — API integration, prompting in code, and the failure modes that only appear in production.
stages.milestone: You can build a .NET service that calls a model API, handles streaming and errors, and evaluates output quality instead of hoping for the best.

steps.note: The capstone of this roadmap — bring everything together in one project.
